items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

ActiveRecord::Base#inspect provides a rich, human-readable representation of model instances with features like attribute filtering, string truncation, and date formatting. However, ActiveModel::Model classes fall back to Ruby's default Object#inspect, which outputs all instance variables in an unhelpful format:

# ActiveRecord - nice output
User.new(name: "Alice").inspect
#=> "#<User id: nil, name: \"Alice\">"

# ActiveModel - falls back to Object#inspect
class Person
  include ActiveModel::Model
  include ActiveModel::Attributes
  attribute :name, :string
end

Person.new(name: "Alice").inspect
#=> "#<Person:0x00007f... @attributes=...>"

Detail

This Pull Request adds ActiveModel::Inspection (included automatically via ActiveModel::Attributes) with full inspection feature parity to ActiveRecord:

  • #inspect - Formatted attribute output: #<Person name: "Alice", age: 30>
  • #full_inspect - Shows all attributes regardless of attributes_for_inspect
  • #pretty_print - Support for pp with proper formatting
  • .filter_attributes - Mask sensitive data with [FILTERED]
  • .attributes_for_inspect - Limit which attributes appear in output
  • String truncation at 50 characters
  • Date/time formatting with to_fs(:inspect)
items.title: Add inspect features to `ActiveModel`

Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because if we set capitalize: true and keep_id_suffix: true, then humanize and titleize methods will display ID instead of Id, as it is more readable, user friendly. Currently it displays Id which is not user friendly.

Detail

Currently, the keep_id_suffix parameter prevents a trailing "_id" from being stripped, but does not capitalize it.

ActiveSupport::Inflector.humanize("author_id", keep_id_suffix: true) # => "Author id"
"author_id".humanize(keep_id_suffix: true) # => "Author id"

This Pull Request changes to

ActiveSupport::Inflector.humanize("author_id", keep_id_suffix: true) # => "Author ID"
"author_id".humanize(keep_id_suffix: true) # => "Author ID"

Which is more user friendly and readable.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

#48823 taught ActiveStorage::Analyzer::AudioAnalyzer to extract the tags metadata from ffprobe. It does this by extracting the tags from the first stream.

However from what I understand and what I've been seeing in practice, ID3 tags like track title, artist name etc. are stored in the container itself, not in the stream, which is returned by ffprobe in the "format" section.

Detail

This Pull Request changes the analyzer to extract the tags from the container rather than the streams, which fixes tags not being picked up for most .mp3s, .flacs etc.

Additional information

I considered merging the tags from the streams and the container but it wasn't exactly clear how duplicate tags should be handled, which looks like can happen in practice.

The test shows how some additional metadata gets picked up from the mp3 in the test fixture.

items.content_html:
Clarify in the Single Table Inheritance guide that the parent model must not be declared as an abstract class.

Motivation / Background

This pull request has been created because STI silently breaks when the parent model is declared as an abstract class. In that case, Active Record does not apply STI semantics and does not automatically populate the type column, which can be confusing and difficult to diagnose. The current guide does not document this constraint, making the misconfiguration easy to introduce.

Detail

This pull request adds a note to the Single Table Inheritance guide clarifying that the STI base class must not be declared as an abstract class.

items.content_html:
The bin/rails server command now binds to :: (all IPv6 interfaces) in non-development environments, instead of 0.0.0.0. The development environment continues to use localhost for backwards compatibility.

IPv6 sockets for :: on most operating systems accept both IPv4 and IPv6 connections, so existing workflows will continue to work. This change prepares Rails for the increasing adoption of IPv6 and reduces reliance on increasingly expensive public IPv4 addresses (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/new-aws-public-ipv4-address-charge-public-ip-insights/).

Here's how different hosts map to different urls:

Host localhost:3000 127.0.0.1:3000 [::1]:3000 0.0.0.0:3000 [::]:3000 Network Open
localhost ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ No
127.0.0.1 ✅ ✅ ❌ ✅ ❌ ❌ No
::1 ✅ ❌ ✅ ❌ ✅ ❌ No
0.0.0.0 ✅ ✅ ❌ ✅ ❌ ✅ Yes
:: ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Yes

This change:

  • 0.0.0.0 => :: (production)

I have a corresponding issue to update the defaults in Puma to IPv6 puma/puma#3812 and a PR puma/puma#3847.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because there is no touch option for ActiveStorage and there are often times that you might not want the parent record touched when the active storage attachment is updated. The touch_attachment_records (#49723) is broad. Sometimes developers need finer grained control.

Detail

This adds a per-attachment touch: option:

  has_one_attached :avatar                   # follows global setting
  has_one_attached :og_image, touch: false   # never touches

The global setting (ActiveStorage.touch_attachment_records) takes precedence if set to false, attachments never touch their parent records regardless of the per-attachment setting.

Reasoning:
The global ActiveStorage.touch_attachment_records setting is broad, affecting all attachments. In some applications, attachments should update the parent's timestamp, while others should not. This allows developers to make that decision on a per attachment basis.

Implementation notes:

  • Changed belongs_to :record to touch: false since Rails evaluates the touch option at class load time, not runtime
  • Override touch method on Attachment to handle conditional cascading
  • Early return in touch_attachments when global is disabled (Attachment has no updated_at column, so touching without cascade is a no-op)

Additional information

Relates to #49723

items.content_html:
Summary

This PR addresses a TODO in activerecord/lib/active_record/fixtures.rb regarding the type expectations of model_class. It ensures that the provided model_class is a subclass of ActiveRecord::Base and provides clearer error messages when an invalid class or a non-existent class name is provided.

Why

The previous implementation accepted any Class object and didn't provide immediate feedback if a string was passed that couldn't be constantized into a class. Enforcing the ActiveRecord::Base requirement prevents potential runtime errors later in the fixture loading process when Active Record specific methods (like table_name or connection_pool) are called on the model class.

What

  • Modified ActiveRecord::FixtureSet#model_class= to:
    • Explicitly check if the class is a subclass of ActiveRecord::Base.
    • Raise an ArgumentError if a string class name is provided but cannot be found.
    • Raise an ArgumentError if the resolved class is not an ActiveRecord::Base descendant.
  • Added comprehensive test cases in activerecord/test/cases/fixtures_test.rb covering:
    • Valid ActiveRecord::Base subclasses (both as Class and String).
    • Invalid non-AR classes.
    • Non-existent class names.

Impact

This change improves developer experience by catching configuration errors in fixtures early with descriptive error messages.
items.title: Clarify and enforce `model_class` type in `ActiveRecord` fixtures

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

URL options should behave the same in tests as they do in actual Rails applications, but they don't.

Detail

Controller's default_url_options should take precedence over the application's default_url_options, but Integration::Session#url_options didn't work in that way.

The BarController in the test is defined as follows:

rails/actionpack/test/controller/integration_test.rb

Lines 918 to 921 in 9248135

class BarController < ActionController::Base
def default_url_options
{ host: "bar.com" }
end

So when you call get "/bar" in the test, the URL helper methods called after that should use bar.com as the host, not foobar.com. But, the test was expecting foobar.com:

rails/actionpack/test/controller/integration_test.rb

Lines 967 to 975 in 9248135

def test_can_override_default_url_options
original_host = default_url_options.dup
default_url_options[:host] = "foobar.com"
assert_equal "http://foobar.com/foo", foos_url
get "/bar"
assert_response :success
assert_equal "http://foobar.com/foo", foos_url
